summary: Masao Abe was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a doctorate from Kyoto University and also studied at Osaka City University, Union Theological Seminary, and Columbia University. He held professorships at Kyoto, Hanazono, and Nara universities.
Masao Sekine worked in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1932 to 1935 and held a post at Tokyo University of Education from circa 1949 to 1976.
Masao Shizutani is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as an assistant professor at Josai University and at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, where his post was attested in 1974.
Masaru Akimoto is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Kyoto Women's University, including as a professor of contemporary society attested in 2002 and later attested in 2015.

Masashi Nagai is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral degrees at Komazawa University. He served Komazawa as lecturer, assistant professor, professor emeritus, and chancellor, and was a chief researcher at the Soto Zen Research Center.

Masataka Suzuki works in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Keio University and held a post there from circa 1980 to 2015. He also served as a lecturer attested at ICPBS and IIBS in 2026.

Masato Kobayashi is a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Kyoto University and completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona. He was a research fellow at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from circa 2000 to 2003.

Masatoshi Konishi worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at International Christian University, the University of Calcutta, the University of Tokyo, and Rikkyo University, and held posts at Hosei University (1971–1984) and Rikkyo University (1984–2003).

Masatoshi Nagatomi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku, Kyoto, and Harvard universities, earning his PhD at Harvard. He held faculty posts at Harvard University starting in 1958 and Harvard Divinity School from circa 1969 to 1996.

Masayuki Taira is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1970 to 1980 and held academic posts at Kansai University, Osaka University, and Kyoto Tachibana University.

Masayuki Tsukimoto is a scholar of Japanology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. His career includes lecturer posts attested in 2026 at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Massimo Pallottino was an Italian archaeologist and historian. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome from circa 1927 to 1931, later holding posts at the University of Cagliari (circa 1940–1945) and Sapienza University of Rome (circa 1947–1980).

Masumi Mochizuki is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Mochizuki held positions at Minobusan University, serving as a faculty of Buddhist studies lecturer (attested 2001), professor (attested 2015), and special appointment professor (attested 2026).

Mathieu Boisvert is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under A. K. Warder and Ravindra Panth. He founded Université du Québec à Montréal and became a professor there in 1992.

Matteo Bartoli was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna from circa 1894 to 1898 and under Heinrich Hübschmann from circa 1898 to 1900. He held an academic post at the University of Turin from circa 1907 to 1946.

Matthew Orsborn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under Guang Xing and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa. In 2026, he was attested as professor and head of international affairs at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Matthew R. Sayers specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Patrick Olivelle and Joel Brereton, and held an academic post at Lebanon Valley College attested in 2013.

Matthew Steven Mitchell works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Osaka City University, the IUC, the University of Hawaiʻi, and Duke University, completing his PhD under Richard M. Jaffe.

Matthew T. Kapstein is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned his PhD from Brown University. He held academic posts at the University of Chicago, Columbia University, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Matthew W. King is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Toronto under Frances Garrett and also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab and Thupten Champa.
